asks: how do I play Aatrox
what's my job as Aatrox
what does Aatrox want to do
aatrox game plan
say: You win long fights by landing Darkin Blade swings and healing off champions, or farm and poke with the first swing when a fight looks bad.
more: Umbral Dash heals you whenever you damage enemy champions, so every swing that lands is damage and health at once. Missed swings mean you are just a slow fighter with no sustain.
Early you want lane priority and short trades that add up. Later you want to be in the middle of fights with World Ender on, where the healing and extra attack damage carry you.
The cost is that you are easy to dodge and easy to kite. If they can walk out of every swing, play the side lane where one target has to face you.
check: Whether your swings are actually landing, and whether the enemy has room to sidestep them.
breaks: If you keep missing or they out-range you, stop forcing full combos; take the wave, poke with the first swing only and wait for a fight where they are slowed or locked down.

asks: when am I strong as Aatrox
is six a big spike for me
can I fight now I have ult
aatrox power spike
say: Level six is your first real all-in: World Ender adds damage, healing and speed, so fight now, or save it to survive their jungler.
more: World Ender raises your attack damage and your healing and lets you run people down. A takedown extends it, so one kill often becomes a second if their jungler arrives late.
Used aggressively it wins the lane outright. Held defensively it turns a gank into a fight you can live through or even win.
Your first completed item on top of level six is the point where trading back into you stops being worth it for most laners.
check: Their health, whether their own ultimate is up, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If they are level six too with a stronger all-in, or the wave is stuck on their side, hold the ultimate and trade short until the wave is in your half.

asks: how do I trade as Aatrox
how do I land my Q
what's the combo in lane
how do I win trades aatrox
say: Trade with Infernal Chains first so they have to walk out, then swing where they run, or just tag them with the first swing for free.
more: Each of the three Darkin Blade swings covers a different area. Umbral Dash moves you mid-swing, so you can shift the area onto them instead of guessing.
Infernal Chains drags them back to the centre and hits again if they do not leave fast. Either they burn movement leaving, or they stand still for your next swing.
Your passive attack heals off their max health, so weave it in when it is ready. Small trades that leave you topped up set up the level six all-in.
check: Whether they still have a dash or a blink to dodge with, and how big the minion wave is on their side.
breaks: If they dodge the chain and step inside your swings, back off and reset rather than finishing a combo that misses; a full miss leaves you with nothing while they hit you freely.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Aatrox
do I go in first
who do I hit in fights
should I flank or front line
say: Walk in second, after someone else starts it, and swing through their front line, or come from the side if their carries have no escape.
more: You heal off every champion you hit, so several enemies in one swing is where you become hard to kill. You are not a tank, though; you need the first stun to land on someone else.
World Ender lasts longer with each takedown. Start it as the fight begins rather than at half health, so the bonus healing covers the whole fight.
A side entrance works when they have no lockdown to stop you. Against heavy crowd control, staying in front of your own carries and punishing whoever dives is the safer line.
check: How much crowd control they have left, and whether your team actually has someone who can start the fight.
breaks: If they kite backwards and you cannot reach anyone, do not chase alone into their team; drop back to your carries and fight whoever comes forward.

when: an enemy has bought a healing-reduction item
asks: they bought anti heal what now
how do I play into grievous wounds
they built anti heal on me
can I still fight with anti heal on them
say: With healing cut, stop relying on long fights: take short trades and wave control, or bring a teammate so the fight ends fast.
more: A lot of your strength is healing off champions and off your empowered attack. When that is reduced, the long brawl you normally win becomes close to even.
The upside is that they spent gold on it instead of on damage or defence. Matching them in farm and pushing the wave still gives you priority for river fights.
In teamfights the reduction only matters on whoever applies it, so pick the targets that are not carrying it when you have the choice.
check: Which enemy holds the item, and whether it applies from their abilities or only their attacks.
breaks: If the laner is far ahead as well, give up the idea of solo kills and play for grouped fights where your swings hit several people at once.

asks: how do I play Bard
what's Bard supposed to do
do I stay in lane as Bard
bard game plan
say: You get strong by leaving lane for chimes and showing up in other fights, or stay bot when your carry can't be left alone.
more: Chimes power up your meeps, so your attacks start hitting an area and slowing. That only comes from walking around the map, which is why you roam more than other supports.
Magical Journey is what makes the roaming cheap: a portal through a wall gets you to mid or river and back faster than walking around.
The trade is your lane partner. Every trip leaves them two against one, so leave on a pushed or reset wave, not while they are being pressured under tower.
check: Where the wave is when you leave, and whether your carry is healthy enough to farm alone for a moment.
breaks: If your carry keeps dying while you are gone, shorten the trips: only take chimes close to lane and stand with them until the lane is stable.

asks: when is Bard strong
what's my spike as Bard
do chimes matter that much
when do I start doing stuff as bard
say: Your spikes are chime counts and level six: grab chimes between waves to upgrade your meeps, or stay and trade if lane is winning.
more: Enough chimes make your meeps deal damage in an area and slow, which turns your basic attacks into real poke. It builds slowly, so missed chimes early cost you later.
Level six gives you Tempered Fate, a long-range stasis. From then on a roam mid or to river can start a fight from far away instead of walking into it.
A winning lane is worth more than a chime. When your carry has the enemy low, staying for the kill beats the walk.
check: Where chimes have appeared near you, and whether the enemy bot lane can punish your carry while you fetch them.
breaks: If the enemy jungler is unaccounted for, skip chimes in the river and only take the ones on your own side.

asks: how do I trade as Bard
how do I land the stun
when do I Q in lane
bard lane tips
say: Throw Cosmic Binding when they stand in front of a wall or line up with a minion, or just hit them with meep attacks.
more: Cosmic Binding only slows the first target on its own. It stuns when it then reaches a wall or a second enemy, and minions count, so angle it through the wave into a champion.
A landed stun is your carry's window to hit freely. A slow is still enough to step up for a meep attack and back off.
Drop Caretaker's Shrine behind your carry early. It heals more the longer it charges, so shrines placed before a trade are worth more than ones placed during it.
check: Where the enemy stands relative to walls and their own minions.
breaks: If they stay in the open with no minion behind them, stop fishing for stuns and save mana; poke with attacks and wait until they walk near the wall.

when: an ally bot laner is alive and you are level 3 or higher
asks: should I roam mid as Bard
when do I leave lane
can I roam now
is it a good time to go mid
say: Roam right after your wave crashes into their tower, through a Magical Journey portal toward mid, or stay if the wave is pushing into you.
more: A crashed wave gives your carry a quiet moment while the next one walks up. That is the cheapest time to disappear, and the enemy mid has the least warning.
A portal through the wall brings you in from an angle they are not watching. Lead with Cosmic Binding into a wall or minion for the stun.
Even a failed roam picks up chimes and makes the mid laner play further back for the next minute. A roam while your wave is under your own tower costs your carry farm or their life.
check: Wave position bot before you go, and whether the enemy mid is pushed up far enough to reach.
breaks: If the enemy support disappears first, do not mirror them blindly; ping it and stay so your carry is not caught alone.

asks: how do I use Bard ult in fights
who do I ult
what do I do in teamfights as Bard
when do I press R
say: Use Tempered Fate on their divers as they jump in, to split the fight, or on their carries first when your team can follow.
more: Tempered Fate puts every champion it touches into stasis, allies included. On their front line it buys your carries time; on their back line it holds targets still for your team's arrival.
The mistake is catching your own team mid-combo and saving the enemy. Aim it where only enemies stand, or at a spot your allies have not reached yet.
After the ultimate, your job is slows from meeps, stuns into walls and shrines dropped where your carries are retreating.
check: Where your own teammates are standing when you cast it, and who on their team is the real threat.
breaks: If your team is already winning the fight, hold it; stasis on a dying enemy only saves them. Keep it for a retreat or the next engage.

asks: can Bard ult the tower
can we dive with my ult
should I ult the turret
how do I help a dive as Bard
say: Tempered Fate freezes turrets too, so drop it on the tower as your team steps in, or on the defender if the dive is short.
more: A turret in stasis does not shoot, which gives your divers a clean window to finish the kill and walk out.
The other use is on the defender: hold them in place while your team gets in position, then everyone hits as stasis ends.
Choose by who is diving. Tanky divers who can take a few tower shots get more from freezing the target; fragile ones need the tower off.
check: Whether the enemy jungler or a teleport can arrive, and that your allies are not inside the area you are about to freeze.
breaks: If their jungler's position is unknown and the wave is thin, skip the dive and take the tower plates or a reset instead.

asks: how do I play Draven
what does Draven want
draven game plan
am I supposed to fight early as Draven
say: You're a lane bully who needs early kills: fight hard with Spinning Axes from level one, or farm up Adoration if their lane out-ranges you.
more: Catching axes keeps your attacks empowered, and every catch and minion adds Adoration. A kill cashes that Adoration in as bonus gold, which is how you get items far ahead of schedule.
The plan is to turn that early gold into towers and dragons before slower carries catch up. Your late game is fine, but it is not where you beat scaling champions.
The cost of playing this hard is that you are pushed up a lot, so your jungler's position and river vision matter more for you than for most carries.
check: Whether your support can start or follow a fight, and where the axes are landing relative to enemy skillshots.
breaks: If the lane is unplayable for fights, stop forcing; farm and keep catching axes so the Adoration is banked for the first kill that does come.

asks: when is Draven strongest
can I fight level one
should we fight at level two
is Draven strong early
say: You're strongest in the first levels: push for level two and fight with two axes spinning, or zone them off the wave if they won't trade.
more: Spinning Axe is a large damage bonus on every attack from level one, when other carries have almost nothing. That gap is biggest in the first few minutes.
Reaching level two first adds Stand Aside for a slow or Blood Rush for speed, and that is usually enough to force summoner spells or a kill.
If they give up the wave instead, you still win: denied farm and a pushed lane is an early plate and a first item lead.
check: Their support's engage range and whether they are stacking the wave to hit level two before you.
breaks: If they reach level two first or their support can lock you down, back off the wave for a moment and fight on the next one instead.

asks: how do I trade as Draven
how do I catch axes safely
where do I put my axes
draven lane tips
say: Trade when the axe will land behind you or to the side, or drop the axe and keep your spacing if it lands forward.
more: The axe falls where you are heading, so move sideways or backwards before attacking to steer it. Walking forward for a catch into their abilities is how lanes get thrown.
Each catch refreshes Blood Rush, so a clean rhythm keeps your attack speed and move speed up for the whole trade.
Keep Stand Aside for their engage. It knocks them aside and slows, which cancels a lot of dives onto you and wins the trade that follows.
check: Where the axe marker lands, and which enemy abilities are aimed at that spot.
breaks: If they throw everything at your catch spot every time, let one axe go; losing an axe costs a little damage, losing the trade costs the lane.

when: you have more kills than deaths and it is before 14:00
asks: I got a kill as Draven what now
how do I use my lead
I'm ahead as Draven what do I do
should I keep fighting or take tower
say: Spend the kill gold right away and come back for tower plates, or move with your support to dragon while their bot is still behind.
more: A kill cashes in your Adoration, so your first item arrives early. The lead is worth most in the next few minutes, before they finish their own item.
Plates and the tower turn a lane lead into gold your whole team keeps. Dragon uses the same lead while their bot lane cannot contest.
Chasing more kills under their tower is the risky version. It pays off the most and it is also how you hand the bounty back.
check: Whether their jungler is on your side of the map, and how much health your support has.
breaks: If their jungler has started camping bot, stop extending; take the farm in front of your tower and let your lead show in the next grouped fight.

when: you have more deaths than kills
asks: I'm behind as Draven
I fed as Draven what do I do
how do I come back as Draven
lane went bad now what
say: Farm safely and keep catching axes so Adoration builds, then cash it on one good fight, or group with your team and hit the front line.
more: Adoration still grows from minions and catches while you are behind, so the next kill pays more than usual. One clean fight can put you back near even.
What you cannot afford is another solo death looking for it. Fight where your team already has numbers or a stun lined up.
Your attacks still hit hard with axes spinning even on fewer items. Playing behind your tanks and hitting whatever is closest is enough to matter.
check: Who on their team can reach you, and whether your team has a fight worth joining nearby.
breaks: If every fight is lost before you arrive, stop walking into them; take side waves near your towers and wait for an enemy mistake.

asks: how do I play Gwen
what does Gwen want
gwen game plan
is Gwen weak early
say: You scale into a duelist who cuts through tanks: farm calmly early, or take short trades when you can land the middle of Snip Snip.
more: A Thousand Cuts deals damage based on the target's health and heals you off champions. The more health they stack, the better your attacks get, which is why you want long games.
Early you are a short-range fighter with little to fall back on. A lane that ends even in farm is a good result.
Later you choose between pressuring a side lane, where few champions can duel you, and joining fights where Hallowed Mist blocks their ranged damage.
check: How the enemy laner trades at short range, and whether you can reach them without eating their whole kit.
breaks: If they bully you off the wave, give up trades entirely and farm with Snip Snip from as far as it reaches until your first item.

asks: when is Gwen strong
when can I fight as Gwen
is six a spike for Gwen
gwen power spike
say: Level six and your first finished item are when you start winning duels: look for an all-in then, or keep farming if you're behind in CS.
more: Needlework slows and applies your passive from range, so at six you can finally start a fight on your terms and stick to the target.
Your first completed item is what makes the health-based damage add up. Before it, long trades into most top laners go badly.
Each item after that widens the gap against tanks and bruisers. If you reach two items even, most side-lane duels are yours.
check: Their level and items compared with yours, and whether their ultimate is available.
breaks: If they hit their own spike first, do not test it; stay near your tower, take the farm and look again after your next item.

asks: how do I trade as Gwen
how do I use Gwen Q
when do I use my W
gwen lane combo
say: Dash in with Skip 'n Slash, land the middle of Snip Snip and step out, or stay and fight inside your mist if they chase.
more: The centre of Snip Snip deals true damage and applies your passive each snip, so the trade is decided by whether they stand in the middle of it.
Skip 'n Slash gives attack speed, range and on-hit damage, and part of its cooldown comes back when you hit something. Use it to enter, then walk out.
Hallowed Mist means enemies outside it cannot target you. Against a laner who has to step in to hit you, that turns their chase into your fight.
check: Whether their main damage is ranged or melee, and how many minions are on each side.
breaks: If they simply walk into the mist with you and win the brawl, stop using it to fight; save it to block their jungler's ranged abilities on a gank.

when: the enemy top laner is a ranged champion
asks: how do I lane against ranged as Gwen
I'm getting poked out as Gwen
ranged top is bullying me
what do I do versus a ranged top
say: Against ranged, farm with Snip Snip and step into Hallowed Mist when they push up to poke, or all-in once you hit six.
more: Enemies outside the mist cannot target you, so a ranged laner has to stop attacking or walk into your range. That is your one comfortable window to farm or to jump on them.
Before six, do not chase. You lose more health walking at them than you deal when you arrive.
After six, Needlework slows from range and Skip 'n Slash closes the gap. A ranged champion without their escape usually loses that fight.
check: Whether their escape or summoner spell is down, and where their jungler could be.
breaks: If they stay too far back to reach even at six, accept an even lane and outscale; a ranged top that cannot kill you is losing by fifteen minutes.

when: you have at least two completed items
asks: should I split as Gwen
do I group or side lane
should I be with my team
can I split push now
say: Push the side lane opposite the next objective and make them send two, or group if your team has no way to stall four against four.
more: Few champions want to duel you in a side lane once you have items, so one defender is usually not enough. Two defenders means your team has the numbers at the objective.
Grouping is the better line when your team needs your damage on their tanks, or when nobody else can start or survive a fight.
Whichever you pick, be there on time. Arriving at the side wave after the objective fight has started gets you neither.
check: Who comes to answer you, how many enemies are missing from the map, and your team's ability to wait.
breaks: If nobody answers you and your team loses the fight anyway, take the tower; if two come and you die, the split was too deep, so push only to the river next time.

asks: how do I play Kai'Sa
what does Kaisa want
kaisa game plan
is Kaisa a late game champ
say: You scale through items that upgrade your abilities: farm to those upgrades, or fight early when your support lands crowd control for your plasma.
more: Second Skin upgrades Icathian Rain, Void Seeker and Supercharge as you buy items. Each upgrade is a real jump, so your game is built around reaching them quickly.
Plasma stacks from your attacks, and your allies' immobilizing effects help stack it. With an engage support you can win early trades that other scaling carries cannot.
Late, Killer Instinct lets you choose where you fight from. That freedom is the reward for a clean laning phase.
check: What kind of support you have, and whether the enemy lane can force fights before your first upgrade.
breaks: If lane is rough, give up trades and take every safe minion; a Kai'Sa even in farm is ahead of schedule.

asks: when is Kaisa strong
when do I evolve my abilities
what's my spike as Kaisa
when can I fight as Kaisa
say: Your spikes come with item purchases that evolve an ability: recall to hit the next upgrade, or stay if a tower plate or dragon is free.
more: The upgraded Icathian Rain fires more missiles, upgraded Void Seeker applies more marks and comes back faster on a champion hit, and upgraded Supercharge adds brief invisibility.
Because the upgrade arrives with the purchase, the timing of your recall matters. Going back slightly early for the piece that completes one is often worth a wave.
Level six adds Killer Instinct. With an upgrade or two it lets you follow a pick anywhere on the screen.
check: Your gold against the next item piece, and where the wave will be when you return.
breaks: If recalling would give up a tower or leave your support alone into a dive, finish the wave first and take the upgrade on the next clean reset.

asks: how do I trade as Kaisa
when do I use Q in lane
how do I stack plasma
kaisa lane tips
say: Trade when your support locks someone down, since that helps stack plasma, or poke with Void Seeker from range if they won't walk up.
more: Plasma builds with each attack and your allies' immobilizing effects help it along, so a stun followed by a few attacks does far more than attacks alone.
Icathian Rain's missiles seek out nearby targets. They tend to land better on a champion who has stepped away from their minions.
Void Seeker is long range and marks what it hits. A landed one makes the next few attacks count for more, so follow it up when it is safe.
check: Whether the enemy is standing inside or away from their minion wave, and if your support's key ability is ready.
breaks: If your support has no crowd control, do not force trades against a stronger lane; farm, poke with Void Seeker and wait for your first upgrade.

asks: what do I do in fights as Kaisa
should I ult in
who do I hit as Kaisa
do I dive the backline
say: Hit the front line from behind your tanks, then use Killer Instinct to finish a marked carry, or dash in early if they're already locked down.
more: Killer Instinct puts you next to an enemy champion. Used late in the fight it cleans up; used first, into a healthy team, it puts a fragile carry in the middle of five.
The early dash is right when a teammate has already caught their carry and your burst ends it before anyone reacts.
Supercharge is your way back out: move speed, and brief invisibility once upgraded. Keep it for after the dash rather than spending it to chase.
check: Which of their crowd control abilities have been used, and how healthy the target is.
breaks: If their lockdown is still unused, do not dash; keep attacking whoever is nearest and let them come to you.

when: your CS is level with or behind the enemy bot laner
asks: how do I scale as Kaisa
should I just farm
lane is even what now
what am I playing for as Kaisa
say: Play for your first ability upgrade: farm every wave and trade only on your support's crowd control, or give a plate rather than die.
more: Each item purchase that evolves an ability changes what you can do in a fight. Getting there on time matters more than winning the two-on-two.
A death costs you a wave and delays the upgrade by a recall. A lost plate costs far less.
Once two abilities are upgraded you can join dragon fights as a real threat. That is the moment to stop farming alone and start moving with your team.
check: The dragon timer and how close you are to the item that completes an upgrade.
breaks: If your team is fighting at an objective and you are nearby, go; scaling does not help if the game is lost four against five.

asks: how do I play Lee Sin
what does Lee Sin want
lee sin game plan
am I supposed to gank a lot as Lee
say: You're strongest early, so make plays before level six pays off for them: gank and skirmish now, or counter their jungler if lanes aren't gankable.
more: Sonic Wave and Resonating Strike close distance, Safeguard jumps to an ally with a shield, and Tempest reveals what it hits. That is a lot of tools at levels where others have few.
The plan is to give your lanes a lead in the first ten minutes and turn it into grubs, herald and dragons. You do not out-scale most junglers, so an even game slowly gets worse.
Later your job narrows to one thing: Dragon's Rage on the right target at the right moment.
check: Which lanes are pushed toward your side, and which of your laners have crowd control to follow up.
breaks: If you fall behind, stop looking for solo fights; clear, ward, and play for one good kick in the next objective fight.

asks: how do I clear as Lee Sin
do I full clear on Lee
what's my first clear
should I gank at three as Lee Sin
say: Clear three camps and look for a level three gank on a pushed lane, or finish all six for level four if nothing's open.
more: After each ability your next two attacks are faster and give energy back. Space your abilities with two attacks between them and you clear smoothly without running dry.
You have your full basic kit at level three, which is earlier than many junglers are ready to fight. That is the reason to consider ganking before the full clear.
A full clear ends around level four as both river crabs appear at 2:55. Arriving there with a level lead is the quieter way to win the early river.
check: Lane states as you finish your third camp, and which side their jungler started.
breaks: If no lane is pushed toward you at level three, do not hover; finish the clear so you are not behind in farm and levels for nothing.

asks: who do I gank as Lee Sin
which lane should I gank
how do I gank on Lee
where's my best gank
say: Gank the lane where your ally has a stun and their wave is thin, or walk in behind them when minions would block Sonic Wave.
more: Sonic Wave stops on the first enemy it meets, minions included. A big wave between you and the target usually means a missed gank, so come from an angle with no minions.
Safeguard dashes to an ally. A laner who has stepped forward is a second gap closer for you, so you can save Sonic Wave until after they use their escape.
Tempest then Cripple keeps them from running. A gank that burns Flash is still a win, since you can return to the same lane on your next pass.
check: Minion positions in that lane, whether the enemy has Flash, and the health of your own laner.
breaks: If your laner is too low to follow or the wave is crashing into their tower, pick another lane or take their jungle camps instead.

asks: what changes at six for Lee Sin
how do I use Lee ult
is level six a spike for Lee
when am I strongest as Lee
say: At six, Dragon's Rage lets you kick a target into your team for a kill, or kick a diver away from your carry.
more: The kick launches the target back and damages enemies they collide with. Get behind them first and it delivers them to your laner or under your tower.
Used the other way, it removes whoever jumped on your carry. That is less flashy and often worth more in a close fight.
Your real peak is the stretch from your first clear to around the first items. Use the ultimate to close out leads then, because later fights give you fewer chances.
check: Where you are standing relative to the target and your team before you press it.
breaks: If you cannot get behind them safely, use the kick for damage or peel instead of forcing a risky reposition.

asks: what do I do late game as Lee Sin
how do I teamfight on Lee
do I go for the carry
what's my job in fights as Lee
say: Late, either kick their carry back into your team from a side angle, or stay near your own carry and kick the first diver away.
more: You do less damage than most champions by this point, so the fight is about where your kick sends one person. A carry kicked into five is a won fight.
Going for it means walking around their front line, and a failed attempt is a four against five. Peeling is the safer choice when your carry is the one who wins the game.
Safeguard's shield on an ally champion and Tempest's reveal are still useful between kicks, especially around brush before an objective.
check: Which enemy carry has no escape left, and whether your carry needs protecting more than theirs needs killing.
breaks: If their carry is always behind three teammates, stop hunting the angle and commit to peeling; do not die before the fight starts.

when: your team has more kills and it is before 14:00
asks: I'm ahead as Lee Sin now what
how do I use my lead as Lee
we won early what next
ganks worked what do I do now
say: Turn the lead into something permanent now: take grubs or dragon with the winning lane, or invade their jungle while their laners can't help.
more: Your advantage shrinks as the game goes on, so kills alone are not enough. Objectives and towers are what still matter at twenty minutes.
Grubs are a single window from 8:00 and do not come back. A dragon returns five minutes after it dies, so each one you take starts the next timer in your favour.
Invading works when the nearby enemy laners are dead or pushed in. Their jungler either gives up camps or fights you while you are stronger.
check: Which lanes have priority, and which enemy laners can rotate to the river first.
breaks: If the lanes next to the objective are losing, do not start it; gank that side first or trade for the other objective.

asks: how do I play Miss Fortune
what does MF want
mf game plan
is MF a lane bully
say: You win lane with poke and win fights with one good Bullet Time: bully with Double Up, or farm and save everything for teamfights.
more: Love Tap adds damage each time you attack a new target, and Double Up bounces to a target behind the first. Both reward switching targets and good angles in lane.
Bullet Time is a channelled cone of heavy damage. Your whole mid game is about finding a spot where several enemies stand in it and nobody can interrupt you.
You have no dash, so your safety is positioning and the move speed from Strut while you are not being hit.
check: Whether the enemy lane has a way to jump on you, and where their support is standing.
breaks: If they have strong engage, stop walking up for poke; stay behind your wave and play for Bullet Time in grouped fights instead.

asks: when is MF strong
is six big for Miss Fortune
can we fight at six
mf power spike
say: Level six is a big jump: fight when they're slowed or stuck in a narrow spot for Bullet Time, or keep it for the dragon fight.
more: Bullet Time hits everything in a cone for its full duration, and each wave can critically strike. Two enemies standing together at half health are in real danger.
In lane it wins the two-on-two if your support can hold them still or they have nowhere to step out. Make It Rain's slow helps keep them inside.
Holding it for the river is the other good use. A narrow river or a pit entrance lines enemies up for you.
check: Whether they have a stun or knock-up that can cancel your channel.
breaks: If their interrupt is still available, wait for it to be used first, or use Bullet Time from behind a teammate where they cannot reach you.

asks: how do I trade as MF
how do I use Double Up
how do I poke as Miss Fortune
mf lane tips
say: Line Double Up through a minion so it bounces into them, or attack the champion then a minion to keep Love Tap ready.
more: Double Up hits a target and then one behind it, and both hits can apply Love Tap. Stand so a minion is between you and them and the bounce does your poking.
